dedupe_keys.name: care eu community database on road accidents resulting in death or injury european road safety observatory

description: CARE is the European Union's database of road crashes that result in death or injury, set up under Council Decision 93/704/EC, which obliges Member States to provide annual accident data. It is managed by the European Commission's Directorate-General for Mobility and Transport within the European Road Safety Observatory, with a CARE expert group of national representatives agreeing the variables, collection, processing and dissemination. Coverage: EU Member States; damage-only accidents are excluded; unlike most international databases it is highly disaggregated, holding detailed records on each accident, the persons and the vehicles involved as collected nationally. Format and access: national authorities upload data through EDAMIS and query the disaggregated records through a data mining system open to national authorities only; the public can use the CARE Dashboard (with a user guide), the Road Safety Atlas, a data glossary of variables and transformation rules, and reference metadata on methodology and quality; free. Licence: not stated on the page read. Caveats: the record-level data are restricted to Member State officials, so outside users see only aggregates through the dashboard and atlas, which were not opened here; national definitions and reporting completeness differ. Simulation uses: crash frequency and severity by road type and user for road safety risk models, hazard exposure of road users and emergency response planning. Related records: the British STATS19 open data (data-gb-road-safety-open-data-stats19) are an example of national record-level crash data of the kind CARE collects.
